subtype: Ex-partner × Sharing private images or messages [Receiver]
passage:
Counsellor's note, Wednesday. Eshaan came in without an appointment and sat at the very edge of the chair. He said his ex, Mridul, still has private pictures and messages from when they were together, and since the breakup Eshaan has been afraid Mridul might share them. No threat has been made, but he can't sleep or concentrate, and he said, "I feel so stupid and ashamed."

I told him that private material being shared without consent is a crime, and that the shame belongs to the person who misuses it, not to him. He looked up at that.

We agreed he'd keep any messages as they are, not delete them, and I helped him plan to speak with his elder cousin tonight. We also talked about how to reach the cyber cell if it ever comes to that. He left looking less alone.

qa.q: What is Eshaan afraid that Mridul might do?
qa.a: He is afraid Mridul might share the private pictures and messages.

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling when he said he felt stupid and ashamed?
qa.a: Fear and shame, together with poor sleep and trouble concentrating, since he worries about the material being leaked.

qa.q: What did the counsellor suggest Eshaan do, and why?
qa.a: Keep the messages as they are, talk to his elder cousin, and know how to reach the cyber cell, because he should not carry this alone and it is a crime, not his shame.

qa.q: How might the counsellor have felt when Eshaan looked up at hearing the shame was not his?
qa.a: The counsellor likely felt encouraged, since his looking up and later leaving less alone showed the reassurance had reached him.

grounding: Shows fear of an ex leaking private material, met with the reminder that it is a crime not shame, keeping evidence, and telling a trusted adult or the cyber cell.

passage:
"Afreen, you've been in your room all day. What happened?"
She turned her phone towards her brother. "Zaid. He says if I don't meet him, he'll send our old chats and a photo to everyone in my class."
Madhav read it twice. His jaw tightened, but his voice stayed low. "Okay. Thank you for showing me."
"I'm so ashamed, bhaiya. I trusted him."
"You trusted someone who is now threatening you. That's his crime, not your shame."
"What if Ammi finds out?"
"We'll tell her together, if you want. First, don't delete anything. Screenshot this, his number, the date."
"Then what?"
"Tonight we file a complaint on the government's cyber crime website, and tomorrow we go to the cyber cell. You don't meet him. You don't reply."
Afreen wiped her face. "You're not angry with me?"
"With you? Never. With him, yes."

qa.q: What did Zaid threaten to do?
qa.a: Send their old chats and a photo to everyone in Afreen's class if she didn't meet him.

qa.q: What was Afreen feeling when she said "I trusted him"?
qa.a: She felt deeply ashamed and frightened, blaming herself for trusting Zaid and worrying about Ammi finding out.

qa.q: Which steps did Madhav suggest, and why do they help?
qa.a: Keep every piece of evidence, never reply or meet Zaid, complain online that night and go to the cyber cell the next day; this protects Afreen and puts the blame on Zaid.

qa.q: How does Madhav see what Zaid did?
qa.a: As Zaid's crime, not Afreen's shame; he is angry with Zaid and calm and protective towards his sister.

grounding: Shows fear that an ex will leak private material, and the wise response of treating it as a crime, keeping evidence and reporting with a trusted family member.

subtype: Ex-partner × Sharing private images or messages [Receiver]
passage:
Last winter, after Harish and I broke up, he posted a story with a blurred picture from a trip we'd taken, captioned "some memories are worth sharing". It showed nothing private, but I knew what else was on his phone. For four days I barely ate. I checked his profile every hour. I told nobody, because I felt foolish for having trusted him at all.
On the fifth day my Masi called and heard it in my voice. I told her everything, crying. She didn't lecture me. She said, "If he shares anything, that is his crime. Your only job now is to keep proof." That evening she sat with me while I saved his post and messages, and the next morning she came with me to the cyber cell to ask how to report.
Nothing was ever leaked. But I learned that carrying it alone was the heaviest part.
— Sarita

qa.q: What caption did Harish put on the story?
Why did Sarita tell nobody for four days?
qa.a: Sarita felt ashamed and foolish for trusting Harish, and was so frightened that eating became hard and checking his profile became hourly.

qa.q: What did Masi do that helped?
qa.a: She listened without lecturing, called any sharing Harish's crime, helped save the post and messages that evening, and went with Sarita to the cyber cell the next morning.

qa.q: What would have changed if Sarita had kept carrying it alone?
qa.a: The fear and hourly checking would likely have gone on, with no proof saved and no report made if Harish did leak something.

grounding: Illustrates fearing an ex will leak private material, the harm of bearing it alone, and the relief of keeping proof and going to the cyber cell with a trusted adult.
